_title: Sagano Romantic Train in Kyoto: Journey Time, Prices and the Best Season to Ride — WoW Train · glosx.app
_desc: The Sagano Romantic Train follows the Hozu River gorge near Kyoto in about 25 minutes. Stations, prices, how to reserve a seat and the best season to ride.
b1: Sagano Romantic Train in Kyoto: Journey Time, Prices and the Best Season to Ride
b2: By WoW Train · October 2026 · 5 min read
b3: The Sagano Romantic Train is a short, slow scenic ride through the Hozu River gorge on the edge of Kyoto. It is not a way to get anywhere fast: it is a 25-minute excursion that fits into a morning in Arashiyama. This guide covers where it runs, how long it takes, what it costs, when to go and how to get a seat.
b4: What it is and where it runs
b5: The line runs between Torokko Saga and Torokko Kameoka, with two stops in between: Torokko Arashiyama and Torokko Hozukyo. The carriages follow the Hozu River gorge, and the operator says the views are worth seeing in all four seasons.
b7: The ride between Saga and Kameoka takes about 25 minutes, so it is easy to add to a day in Arashiyama. The train is slow on purpose: you pay for the view, not the speed.
b9: The operator charges one fare no matter how far you ride. Adults are 12 and over, and children from 6 to 12 pay the child fare. Kyoto tourist listings show about ¥880 for adults and ¥440 for children one way, but confirm the current price on the operator's site before you go, because fares can change. Infants under 1 ride free; a very young child who takes a seat needs a child ticket.
b11: The gorge changes with every season. Spring, with cherry blossoms, and autumn, with red leaves, are the most popular times and also the busiest: weekends and holidays in those weeks sell out early. Autumn colour in Kyoto usually peaks around late November and cherry blossoms around late March to early April, but it shifts every year, so check the forecast. For fewer crowds, choose a weekday or an early departure.
b13: Reserve online on the operator's site: choose the date, direction and number of passengers (up to 8), then pick your car and seat. You need to register an account.
b14: Pay by credit card. The ticket arrives by email and you show a QR code at the gate.
b15: Same-day tickets are sold at the station counters on a first-come basis (not at Torokko Hozukyo), and a limited number of standing tickets are sold once the seats run out.
b16: Check the calendar before you go
b17: The train does not run every day of the year. The operator publishes a yearly calendar and timetable, including the closed days, so check them for your dates. We do not list departure times here because they change with the season.
b19: The Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is nearby and is the classic pairing with the train.
b20: Plan your return: many visitors ride one way on the Romantic Train and come back by the JR line or on a Hozu River boat ride (check the boat's operating dates).
b21: Kyoto is connected to Osaka and Tokyo by Shinkansen, so the train fits easily into a bigger itinerary.
